models_evaluated: DenseNet-121 deep learning ARDS detection model

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI-first strategy deferring uncertain cases to physicians vs AI alone or physician alone
links.effect: AI deferring to physician if uncertain: accuracy 0.869 (0.835-0.903) vs AI alone 0.847 and physician alone 0.808; physician review burden only 20.7%.
links.quote: The physician-aided AI strategy, which defers the diagnosis to physicians only if the AI model is uncertain, resulted in improved diagnostic accuracy than both physician- and AI-alone.

links.outcome: Accuracy of physician-AI collaboration strategies versus physician alone and AI alone
links.effect: Collaboration strategies achieved 0.824-0.871 accuracy vs physician alone 0.808; physician-aided AI beat physician alone for 8/9 physicians, significantly for 3/9. Overreliance not assessed; physicians not shown AI output.
links.quote: For 8/9 physicians the physician-aided AI strategy outperformed the physician’s alone accuracy.

links.outcome: AI model accuracy compared with physicians on the same chest X-rays
links.effect: AI accuracy 0.847 (0.806–0.887) vs physicians 0.808 (0.767–0.85), p<0.05; sensitivity 0.789 vs 0.727.
links.quote: Overall, the deep learning-based AI system had significantly higher accuracy in detecting ARDS images compared to physicians (0.847 [95% CI 0.806–0.887] vs. 0.808 [95% CI 0.767–0.85], p value of < 0.05 using the one-sided bootstrapped two-sample hypothesis testing) (Table 2 ).

links.outcome: Accuracy when physicians review only AI-uncertain cases versus all cases
links.effect: Physician review of only 20.8% of X-rays gave accuracy 0.869, near the weighted average requiring review of all (0.871); AI-only 0.847. Accuracy fell to 0.596 for AI in AI-uncertain cases.
links.quote: The weighted average of physician and AI model only marginally exceeded that of the physician-aided AI strategy, and would require physicians to review every chest X-ray.

links.outcome: Whether AI confidence/uncertainty corresponds to accuracy and can be used to defer
links.effect: AI accuracy rose with confidence; accuracy was 0.596 in AI-uncertain images, where physicians reached 0.698, enabling deferral.
links.quote: The AI model’s accuracy increased as its confidence increased, suggesting that the AI model is capable of recognizing when it is uncertain (green line in Fig. 1c ).

unlisted_practices: Comparing AI-first-with-deferral, physician-first-with-AI-fallback, averaged and weighted-average human-AI combination strategies
Using AI as an audit tool with second-physician over-read when AI and physician disagree

models_evaluated: 121-layer DenseNet ARDS chest X-ray detection model

links.quote: Overall, the deep learning-based AI system had significantly higher accuracy in detecting ARDS images compared to physicians (0.847 [95% CI 0.806–0.887] vs. 0.808 [95% CI 0.767–0.85], p value of < 0.05 using the one-sided bootstrapped two-sample hypothesis testing) (Table 2 ).

links.effect: AI-first deferral accuracy 0.869, higher than physician-alone 0.808 and AI-alone 0.847; weighted average accuracy 0.871.
links.quote: Among several collaboration strategies tested, we find that if the AI model first reviews the chest X-ray and defers to a physician if it is uncertain, this strategy achieves a higher diagnostic accuracy (0.869, 95% CI 0.835-0.903) compared to a strategy where a physician reviews a chest X-ray first and defers to an AI model if uncertain (0.824, 95% CI 0.781-0.862), or strategies where the physician reviews the chest X-ray alone (0.808, 95% CI 0.767-0.85) or the AI model reviews the chest X-ray alone (0.847, 95% CI 0.806-0.887).

links.effect: Physician-aided AI accuracy 0.869 [95% CI 0.835–0.903] and review burden 20.7 (15.8, 25.8), reducing manual review by 79.2%.
links.quote: Having the AI model interpret a chest X-ray first and defer to the physician if it is uncertain has near-equivalent accuracy, while reducing the number of chest X-rays that required manual physician review to determine if ARDS is present by 79.2%.

links.effect: AI accuracy increased with confidence; when AI was uncertain in 20.8% of images, physicians accuracy 0.698 [95% CI 0.623–0.767] vs AI 0.596 [95% CI 0.498–0.695].
links.quote: The AI model’s accuracy increased as its confidence increased, suggesting that the AI model is capable of recognizing when it is uncertain (green line in Fig. 1c ).

unlisted_practices: Physician-first deferral to AI when the physician is uncertain
Averaging or weighted averaging physician and AI diagnostic scores
Using AI-physician disagreement to trigger second physician over-read

links.outcome: diagnostic accuracy and physician review burden of uncertainty deferral
links.effect: Diagnostic accuracy was 0.869 (95% CI 0.835-0.903) with AI deferral of uncertain cases to physicians, versus 0.847 (0.806-0.887) for AI alone and 0.808 (0.767-0.85) for physician alone, requiring review in 20.7% of cases.
links.quote: Among several collaboration strategies tested, we find that if the AI model first reviews the chest X-ray and defers to a physician if it is uncertain, this strategy achieves a higher diagnostic accuracy (0.869, 95% CI 0.835-0.903) compared to a strategy where a physician reviews a chest X-ray first and defers to an AI model if uncertain (0.824, 95% CI 0.781-0.862), or strategies where the physician reviews the chest X-ray alone (0.808, 95% CI 0.767-0.85) or the AI model reviews the chest X-ray alone (0.847, 95% CI 0.806-0.887).

AI auditing with second clinician review upon AI-clinician disagreement
